transcripts.title: Brightloom Kirana quarterly board call
transcripts.text:

Location: Bengaluru. Attendees: Anaya Vermillion (CEO), Meera Thistlewood (COO), Vikram Ollandry (chair), Thornfield Partners (investor).



ANAYA VERMILLION: We tightened the onboarding checklist after the last cohort and the time-to-first-value has come down noticeably since then. Several enterprise accounts have asked for a full security review before they will commit to a renewal, which is adding weeks to those cycles. Our main competitor has been unusually quiet in the market, although we hear from candidates that they are rebuilding their platform.

MEERA THISTLEWOOD: We introduced a formal incident review process and the recurring causes have become much easier to see. Localisation has come up repeatedly in the enterprise segment but we have deferred it until the core is stable. Contract negotiations with our largest supplier are ongoing and we expect better terms given the volume commitment.

ANAYA VERMILLION: Partner-sourced pipeline is growing slowly but the quality of those introductions has been consistently higher. The engineering team has asked to reduce on-call load next quarter and we think that is reasonable given the release cadence. Support volumes have been steady and the escalation path we introduced last quarter is working much better than the old rota.

MEERA THISTLEWOOD: The team offsite is booked and the agenda is mostly product strategy with a short session on operating cadence. We deprecated the older integration surface after giving customers a long migration window and there was little pushback. We moved the weekly release window to give the QA team a clear day before anything ships to production.

VIKRAM OLLANDRY: Noted. Anything else on that?

ANAYA VERMILLION: On the topline, we closed the quarter at an ARR of ₹5.5 crore. That's separate from the ₹6.4 crore Series A we banked earlier in the year.

MEERA THISTLEWOOD: We have started publishing a changelog externally and customers have responded well to the increased visibility. The design partner programme continues to be the most useful input we have for prioritising the roadmap. The hiring loop is taking longer than we would like, and most of the drop-off is happening at the final onsite stage rather than earlier in the funnel.

ANAYA VERMILLION: Candidate quality for senior engineering roles has improved since we started publishing more technical writing. Recruiting for the finance role is open and we have a shortlist, though the market for that profile is competitive. Procurement cycles in the public sector remain slow and difficult to forecast, so we have stopped putting them in the near-term pipeline.

MEERA THISTLEWOOD: The compliance certification process is underway and the auditor has asked for additional evidence on access control. Internal tooling for the support team was built in-house, which was faster than evaluating vendors for that workflow. Churn conversations are being handled by the founders directly for now, because the signal from those calls is worth the time.

ANAYA VERMILLION: The account management function is still shared between the founders, which is not sustainable much beyond this year. We rewrote the onboarding documentation after the last round of user interviews and the support tickets about setup have dropped away. Our infrastructure spend has been reviewed line by line and we found meaningful savings in unused reserved capacity.

VIKRAM OLLANDRY: Thanks, that's helpful context.

MEERA THISTLEWOOD: Looking at growth, revenue is up 115% year on year. Month on month we're running at about 4%.
